mainTopic: רבי שמעון's view on טומאה for non-food items, the six intentions for slaughtering a קרבן, and slaughtering a חטאת for the sake of חולין
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why the תורה mentions כרת three times for eating קדשים while טמא, and shows that for רבי שמעון the third mention teaches about the inner חטאות. It then quotes רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה, that there is liability for טומאה only on items normally eaten, and brings a dispute among two pairs of אמוראים about how far that argument reaches. There are two versions of this dispute, from רב טביומי and from רב כהנא. רבא decides that רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue both about impure items and about an impure person, and the גמרא explains that the word 'והבשר' only gives wood and frankincense a minor disqualification. A new משנה then lists the six intentions a קרבן is slaughtered for, and רבי יוסי says the קרבן is valid even with none of them in mind. רב explains these intentions from the words of the פסוק and rules that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of חולין is valid. רבה challenges him from רבי יוסי, and אביי answers that such a קרבן is valid but does not bring atonement. Finally, רבי אלעזר separates slaughtering 'for the sake of' חולין, which is valid, from slaughtering 'as' חולין, which is disqualified, and begins to bring a supporting question from שמואל to רב הונא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Three mentions of כרת, three jobs
steps.stepSummary: Each of the three mentions of כרת for eating קדשים while טמא teaches something different: a כלל, a פרט, and items that are not usually eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: One mention is for the general rule, one is for the detail, and one is for things that are not normally eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to why the תורה repeats כרת three times about eating קדשים while טמא. Each mention gets its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first mention gives a broad general rule (כלל). The second gives a specific detail (פרט), and through it the rule is applied to all קדשים offered on the מזבח. The third adds a new case: even items that people do not normally eat, like wood and לבונה, bring כרת if eaten while טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Being 'cut off', a heavenly punishment
A general statement or rule
A specific detail
Items that are not normally eaten
Ritual impurity

phrases.english: One is for a generalization, and one is for a detail,
phrases.notes: These are the three mentions of כרת about eating קדשים while טמא (ויקרא 7:20–21, 22:3).

phrases.english: and one is for items that are not eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun before this section, about why there are three mentions of כרת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three mentions are for a כלל, a פרט, and non-food items.

steps.title: What does the third mention teach for רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds there is no טומאה liability for non-food items, so the third mention of כרת cannot be teaching about them. What does it teach for him?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי שמעון, who says that for things that are not eaten one is not liable because of טומאה, what does the third mention come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. The third mention of כרת was used for non-food items, but רבי שמעון does not accept that rule, so what is it for in his view?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון exempts someone who eats non-food items while טמא. That leaves the third mention of כרת with no job in his view. The question is what it adds instead.

keyTerms.meaning: To include what?
Liable to punishment

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon, who says:
items that are not eaten,
one is not liable for them because of impurity,
what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the three-way breakdown from step 1 against רבי שמעון's opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the third mention of כרת teaches according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: It includes the inner חטאות
steps.stepSummary: For רבי שמעון, the third mention of כרת includes חטאות whose blood is brought inside the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the inner חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: for רבי שמעון, the extra mention teaches that the inner חטאות also bring כרת if eaten while טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאות הפנימיות are חטאות whose blood is sprinkled inside, not on the outer מזבח. The third mention is used to bring them into the טומאה punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Inner חטאות, whose blood is brought inside the היכל

phrases.english: To include the inner sin offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The third mention includes the inner חטאות.

steps.title: Why the inner חטאות need a special source
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that since רבי שמעון exempts inner offerings from פיגול, he also exempts them from טומאה. The extra mention teaches that he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since רבי שמעון says that anything not offered on the outer מזבח like שלמים has no פיגול liability, it should also have no טומאה liability. So the תורה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the inner חטאות needed their own source, by showing the mistake we would otherwise have made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that פיגול only applies to offerings handled like שלמים, whose blood goes on the outer מזבח. We could have extended that limit to טומאה as well. The extra mention of כרת blocks that comparison, so טומאה applies to the inner חטאות even though פיגול does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It might have entered your mind to say
An offering made invalid by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten
The outer altar
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, inner חטאות are exempt from פיגול but still carry כרת for טומאה. The third mention of כרת teaches this.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say,
since Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן כִּשְׁלָמִים –
phrases.english: anything that is not on the outer altar like peace offerings,
phrases.notes: He means offerings whose blood is not put on the outer מזבח the way שלמים blood is.

phrases.english: one is not liable for it because of piggul,
then one should also not be liable because of impurity;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the answer in step 3 is needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because רבי שמעון exempts inner offerings from פיגול, they might also be exempt from טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra כרת teaches that inner חטאות do carry טומאה liability.

steps.title: Quoting רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה where רבי שמעון makes one liable only for items that are normally eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון makes one liable for something that is normally eaten, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the line of the משנה it is about to discuss. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון makes a טמא person liable only for eating things that are normally eaten, not wood, לבונה or קטורת. The חכמים make him liable in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: Something normally eaten
And so on

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon stated:
he deems liable for that which is normally eaten, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוּמִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְחַיֵּיב אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון makes one liable for טומאה only for items normally eaten.

steps.title: Two pairs of אמוראים disagree
steps.stepSummary: A dispute is reported between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, and between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, with one member of each pair on each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. One opinion is held by one from this pair and one from that pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a dispute among the אמוראים about רבי שמעון's ruling. It names who disagrees, and the actual opinions come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair is split. One member of each pair holds the first opinion, and the other member holds the second. The גמרא does not say here which person says which.

keyTerms.meaning: A pair

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think each pair agrees with itself. Each pair is split, with one member on each side.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא –
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina:

phrases.aramaic: חַד מֵהַאי זוּזָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּזָא;
phrases.english: one from this pair and one from that pair;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a dispute about the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the people in the dispute; the two opinions follow in steps 7 and 8.

steps.title: First view: the dispute is only about impure meat
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא says the רבנן and רבי שמעון argue only when the wood or frankincense itself became impure. When the person eating is impure, everyone agrees there is no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: One says: the dispute is about impurity of the meat. But when the person's body is impure, everyone agrees he is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the first side of the argument from step 6. This view limits the dispute to the case where the item that is eaten is impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of impurity here. In טומאת בשר, the food itself is impure. In טומאת הגוף, the person eating is impure. This view says the רבנן hold one is flogged for eating impure wood or frankincense. But no one, not even the רבנן, gives lashes to an impure person who eats them.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of the item being eaten (the 'meat' itself is impure)
Impurity of the person's body (the one eating is impure)
Everyone agrees
Receives lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two impurities. 'Impure meat' means the food is impure. 'Impure body' means the person eating is impure.

phrases.english: One says:
The dispute is about impurity of the meat,
but with impurity of the body,
everyone agrees he is not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the content of the first opinion from the dispute introduced in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is limited to טומאת בשר. For טומאת הגוף, all agree there are no lashes.

steps.title: Second view: the dispute covers both cases, with a reason
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says the argument applies equally to impure meat and to an impure person. His reason is that the two פסוקים go together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one says: just as there is a dispute in this case, so there is a dispute in that case. Why? Since the verse 'and the meat that touches anything impure' applies to these items, the next verse 'with his impurity upon him' applies to them too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposing view and explains it. This view says the dispute covers both kinds of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן include wood and frankincense in the פסוק about impure meat (ויקרא ז:יט). This view says that if that פסוק covers them, the very next פסוק, about an impure person eating (ויקרא ז:כ), covers them too. So the רבנן give lashes in both cases, and רבי שמעון exempts in both.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as they argue in this case, so they argue in that case
We read (apply) the verse to it
'With his impurity upon him': the verse about an impure person eating קדשים

phrases.english: And one says:
As there is a dispute in this case,
so there is a dispute in that case.
What is the reason?
Since we read about it
"And the meat that touches anything impure,"
we also read about it "with his impurity upon him."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:20. This is the very next פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: כְּמַחְלוֹקֶת בָּזוֹ כָּךְ מַחְלוֹקֶת בָּזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to step 7, along with a reason based on the פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies to both טומאת בשר and טומאת הגוף, because the two neighboring פסוקים apply together.

steps.title: רב כהנא's different version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports the argument differently and places it on רבי שמעון's clause. One view says the dispute is only about an impure person, and everyone agrees there is lashes for impure meat. The other view says the dispute is about both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טביומי teaches it the way we just learned. רב כהנא teaches it differently. One from each pair spoke about the latter clause. One says: the dispute is about an impure body, but for impure meat everyone agrees he is flogged. The other says: just as there is a dispute in this case, so in that case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us there is a second version of this whole argument. In it, the 'limited' view flips: the dispute is only about the impure person, not the impure meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב כהנא's version, the argument centers on רבי שמעון's statement. The limited view says רבי שמעון exempts only an impure person who eats wood or frankincense. Even רבי שמעון agrees there is lashes for eating these items when they themselves are impure. The 'both cases' view stays the same as before.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way (reports the discussion in this version)
A pair
On the latter clause

steps.confusionAlert: In רב טביומי's version, everyone agrees there is no lashes for an impure person. In רב כהנא's version, everyone agrees there IS lashes for impure meat. The limited view is reversed between the two versions.

phrases.english: Rav Tavyumei teaches it this way;
Rav Kahana teaches it this way:

phrases.aramaic: חַד מֵהַאי זוּזָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּזָא
phrases.english: One from this pair and one from that pair
phrases.notes: The pairs are רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, and רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, from step 6.

phrases.english: on the latter clause:
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה, quoted in step 5.

phrases.english: One says: the dispute is about impurity of the body,
but with impurity of the meat,
everyone agrees he is flogged;
and one says:
As there is a dispute in this case, so there is a dispute in that case.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב טָבְיוֹמֵי מַתְנֵי הָכִי; רַב כָּהֲנָא מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the dispute presented in steps 7 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב כהנא's version, one view says the dispute is only about טומאת הגוף, and all agree there is lashes for טומאת בשר. The other view says they argue about both.

steps.title: רבא: the 'both cases' view makes the most sense
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules in favor of the view that the dispute covers both cases. His reason: since רבי שמעון does not apply the impure-person פסוק to these items, he does not apply the impure-meat פסוק to them either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it makes sense to follow the one who says that just as there is a dispute in this case, so there is a dispute in that case. Why? Since we do not apply 'with his impurity upon him… shall be cut off' to these items, we also do not apply 'and the meat that touches anything impure shall not be eaten' to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא weighs in and picks a side. He says the view that the dispute covers both cases is more logical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both versions, רבי שמעון exempts an impure person who eats wood or frankincense, so the impure-person פסוק does not cover these items for him. רבא reasons that the two פסוקים go together. So if the second פסוק doesn't apply, the first doesn't either. That means רבי שמעון exempts impure meat too, so he argues with the רבנן in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes sense
Like the one who says
'Shall be cut off': the punishment of כרת

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the dispute (רב טביומי and רב כהנא). Each has a 'limited' view and a 'both cases' view. רבא prefers the 'both cases' view: the two פסוקים in ויקרא ז stand or fall together.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא uses the same 'the two פסוקים go together' logic as step 8, but in reverse. Step 8 said: if the first פסוק applies, so does the second. רבא says: if the second does not apply, neither does the first.

phrases.english: Rava said: It stands to reason
like the one who says
as there is a dispute in this case, so there is a dispute in that case.
What is the reason?
Since we do not read about it
"with his impurity upon him… shall be cut off,"
we do not read about it

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּכׇל טָמֵא לֹא יֵאָכֵל״.
phrases.english: "And the meat that touches anything impure shall not be eaten."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the opinions in steps 7 to 9 and sides with the 'both cases' view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי שמעון, eating wood or frankincense brings no lashes for impurity at all, whether the item or the person is impure. The two פסוקים apply together or not at all.

steps.title: Challenge: the word 'and the flesh' includes wood and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling by quoting a teaching that the word 'והבשר' includes wood and frankincense.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master teach that the word 'and the flesh' comes to include wood and frankincense?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's ruling from Step 10 by quoting a teaching that the impure-meat פסוק does cover wood and frankincense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that רבי שמעון does not apply the impure-meat פסוק to wood and frankincense. But a teaching says the extra word 'והבשר' was written to include them. That seems to put them right inside the impure-meat law.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say? This introduces a known teaching used as a challenge.
To include. An extra word in the פסוק adds something to the law.
Wood (for the altar) and frankincense.

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
"And the flesh" comes to include wood and frankincense!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's conclusion in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the impure-meat פסוק does not apply to wood and frankincense.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching directly says 'והבשר' includes wood and frankincense, so the impure-meat law seems to apply to them.

steps.title: Answer: the inclusion is only for disqualification
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'והבשר' includes wood and frankincense only to make them disqualified, not for lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: That inclusion is merely for disqualification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the teaching only means wood and frankincense become disqualified when impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'והבשר' does not bring wood and frankincense into the full law with lashes. It only teaches that they become פסול when impure, and this disqualification is a rabbinic one that the פסוק merely supports. So רבא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: For disqualification; the item becomes פסול.
Merely; only this and nothing more.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא's reading of רבי שמעון, wood and frankincense can become פסול through טומאה, but there are no lashes for them under either the impure-meat פסוק or the impure-person פסוק. The רבנן disagree.

phrases.english: It is merely for disqualification.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean about the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the quoted teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The inclusion from 'והבשר' means wood and frankincense carry the full impure-meat law with lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The inclusion only makes them פסול, so רבא's ruling is not contradicted.

steps.title: The משנה: six intentions for slaughtering a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists six things a קרבן is slaughtered for the sake of, plus 'for the sake of sin' for a חטאת and an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A קרבן is slaughtered for the sake of six things: for the sake of the offering, for the sake of the owner, for the sake of ה׳, for the sake of the altar fires, for the sake of the aroma, and for the sake of the pleasing. A חטאת and an אשם are also for the sake of the sin.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the six things a person should have in mind when slaughtering a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names six intentions: the type of offering, the owner, ה׳, burning on the fires, aroma, and pleasing. A חטאת and an אשם also have a seventh intention: for the sin they atone for.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of; with this in mind.
Here, the owner who brings the קרבן.
The fires of the altar.
A pleasing aroma; the משנה counts ריח and ניחוח as two separate intentions.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ לְשֵׁם שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים הַזֶּבַח נִזְבָּח:
phrases.english: MISHNA: The offering is slaughtered for the sake of six things:
for the sake of the offering, for the sake of the one offering it,
phrases.notes: 'The one offering it' means the owner of the קרבן, not the person doing the slaughtering.

phrases.english: for the sake of God, for the sake of the fires,
for the sake of the aroma, for the sake of the pleasing.
And the sin offering and guilt offering are for the sake of the sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לְשֵׁם שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים הַזֶּבַח נִזְבָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the end of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרבן is slaughtered with six intentions in mind, and a חטאת and an אשם also for the sake of the sin.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a קרבן is valid even with none of these intentions
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says a קרבן slaughtered without any of these intentions is still valid, because of a rule made by the court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: Even someone who had none of these in mind, the קרבן is valid. This is a rule of the court, because the intention goes only after the one doing the service.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds that the קרבן is still valid even if the person had none of the six intentions in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The six intentions are not required for the קרבן to be valid. The court's stipulation (תנאי בית דין) is that the one slaughtering should not state any intention at all. Since the intention follows only the one doing the עבודה, a wrong intention from him could ruin the קרבן, so it is safer to have none.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule or condition set by the court.
Intention; what the person has in mind during the עבודה.
The one doing the service.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not saying the wrong intention is fine. He is saying that having no particular intention at all does not ruin the קרבן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
Even one who did not have in his heart
any one of all these, it is valid;
for it is a stipulation of the court,
since the intention does not go
except after the one performing the service.
phrases.notes: He means only the person doing the service has the power to affect the קרבן with his thoughts, not the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אַף מִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּלִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the list in Step 13: the intentions are not required after the fact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרבן slaughtered without any of the listed intentions is valid, based on a court rule, because the intention follows the one doing the service.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the list of six intentions is the proper way to do things, but leaving them out does not make the קרבן פסול.

steps.title: רב: what 'for the sake of an עולה' and 'for the sake of the fires' exclude
steps.stepSummary: רב explains two items from the משנה's list by showing what each one excludes: an עולה slaughtered as a שלמים, and roasting instead of burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: 'An עולה' means for the sake of an עולה, to exclude slaughtering it for the sake of a שלמים, which is not allowed. 'Fires' means for the sake of the altar fires, to exclude roasting, which is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. רב shows what two of the intentions come to rule out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'For the sake of the offering' means the right type: an עולה must not be done as a שלמים. 'For the sake of the fires' means it must be meant for burning on the altar, not for roasting to eat. Each item in the list rules out a wrong intention.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to rule out.
Peace offering, which is mostly eaten by the owners.
Roasting meat to eat it, like a kabob.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
"A burnt offering" means for the sake of a burnt offering,
to exclude for the sake of a peace offering, which is not allowed.
"Fires" means for the sake of the fires,
to exclude roasting, which is not allowed.
phrases.notes: Roasting means cooking meat to eat it, instead of burning it up on the altar as an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: ״עוֹלָה״ – לְשֵׁם עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's explanation of the list in the משנה of Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'For the sake of the offering' excludes slaughtering an עולה as a שלמים; 'for the sake of the fires' excludes intending to roast it.

steps.title: The word 'aroma' excludes limbs that were roasted first
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that 'ריח' means the burning must be for the sake of aroma. This excludes limbs that were roasted first and only then put on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Aroma' means for the sake of aroma. This excludes limbs that someone roasted and then brought up to the altar, which does not count. As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: limbs that were roasted and then brought up do not count as aroma.
steps.whatsHappening: רב continues going through the משנה's list. Now he explains the word 'ריח' and backs it up with a ruling he said elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering has to produce a 'pleasing aroma' when it burns on the מזבח. If the limbs were roasted before being put on the fire, they no longer give that aroma. So the intention 'for the sake of aroma' rules out that way of doing it.

keyTerms.meaning: Aroma: the smell of the offering burning on the מזבח
To exclude; this word comes to rule out a certain case
The limbs of the animal that are burned on the מזבח
That he roasted them and then brought them up to the מזבח

phrases.english: "Aroma": for the sake of aroma,
to exclude limbs that one roasted and then brought up to the altar, which does not count.
As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Limbs that one roasted and then brought up to the altar,
do not count as aroma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's word-by-word explanation of the משנה's list from Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'For the sake of aroma' excludes limbs that were roasted before being burned, since they give no proper aroma.

steps.title: The meaning of 'pleasing' and 'to ה''
steps.stepSummary: רב explains the last two items: 'ניחוח' means for the sake of pleasing God's spirit, and 'לה'' means for the sake of the One Who spoke and the world came into being.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Pleasing' means for the sake of giving satisfaction. 'To ה'' means for the sake of the One Who spoke and the world came into being.
steps.whatsHappening: רב finishes explaining the משנה's list with the last two words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier items, רב does not say what these two rule out. He just gives their meaning: the offering should please God, and it must be meant for God alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Pleasing
Giving satisfaction or contentment to God
The One Who spoke and the world came into being: a name for God

steps.whatToRemember: רב reads the words of ויקרא 1:9 ('עולה', 'אשה', 'ריח', 'ניחוח', 'לה׳') as the sources for the intentions listed in the משנה.

phrases.english: "Pleasing": for the sake of giving satisfaction.
"To the Lord": for the sake of the One Who spoke and the world came into being.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the list that began in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ניחוח' means to please God; 'לה'' means the offering is for God alone.

steps.title: A חטאת slaughtered as an עולה is disqualified, but as חולין it is valid
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of an עולה is disqualified, but if it was slaughtered for the sake of חולין, it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A חטאת that someone slaughtered for the sake of an עולה is disqualified. For the sake of non-holy meat, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב about the wrong kind of intention when slaughtering a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a חטאת slaughtered for a different קרבן is completely disqualified. רב adds that this only happens when the wrong intention is for another holy offering. If he intended plain non-holy meat, the חטאת stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
Burnt offering
Ordinary, non-holy animals or meat
Disqualified / valid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume every wrong intention disqualifies a חטאת. Intending it for a different קרבן disqualifies it, but intending it for the sake of חולין does not. This is not about someone who really thinks the animal is ordinary. Step 22 rules that such a case (משום חולין) is disqualified.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering is disqualified.
For the sake of a non-sacred animal, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: חַטָּאת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ לְשֵׁם עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the משנה's theme of intentions during slaughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת slaughtered for another קרבן is disqualified; slaughtered for the sake of חולין, it remains valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling becomes the target of רבה's challenge in the next steps.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's source for רב: only holy things ruin holy things
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains רב's reason from the פסוק 'ולא יחללו את קדשי בני ישראל': holy intentions can ruin a קרבן, but non-holy intentions cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: What is רב's reason? 'And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel.' Holy things profane holy things, but non-holy things do not profane holy things.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks for the source of רב's ruling and answers it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about 'profaning the holy things.' רבי אלעזר reads it as meaning that a holy intention, like another קרבן, can ruin a holy offering. An intention of plain חולין has no power to ruin it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
They will profane or ruin something holy
Holy things; here, an intention for another קרבן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב?
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: What is the reason of Rav?
"And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel":
holy things profane holy things,
but non-sacred things do not profane holy things.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רב's ruling in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a חולין intention does not disqualify a חטאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 22:15, read as: only holy things profane holy things.

steps.title: רבה challenges רב from רבי יוסי's statement
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רבי יוסי, who said a קרבן is valid when the person had none of the intentions in mind. רבה infers that if he had חולין in mind, it would be disqualified, which goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה raised an objection: רבי יוסי says, even one who did not have in mind any one of these intentions, the קרבן is valid, because it is a rule of the court. The reason is that he had nothing at all in mind. But if he had in mind non-holy meat, it would be disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב's ruling using the words of רבי יוסי from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said the קרבן is valid when the person had nothing in mind. רבה reads this closely: it is valid only because he had nothing in mind. That suggests an intention of חולין would disqualify it, the opposite of what רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule set by the court
In his heart; in his mind
The reason is... but otherwise: a way of reading what a statement implies

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection:
Rabbi Yosei says:
Even one who did not have in mind
any one of all these intentions, it is valid,
since it is a rule of the court.
The reason it is valid is that he had nothing in mind at all,

phrases.aramaic: הָא הָיָה בְּלִבּוֹ לְשֵׁם חוּלִּין – פָּסוּל!
phrases.english: but if he had in mind for the sake of a non-sacred animal, it is disqualified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from Step 18, which רבי אלעזר explained in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of חולין is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי makes validity depend on having no intention at all, which implies a חולין intention would disqualify the קרבן.

steps.title: אביי: A חולין Thought Means Valid but No Atonement
steps.stepSummary: אביי defends רב by reading רבי יוסי differently. With no intention at all, the קרבן is valid and brings atonement. With a חולין intention, it is still valid but does not bring atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Maybe רבי יוסי means this. If he had no intention at all, the קרבן is valid and brings atonement. But if he had חולין in mind, it is valid but does not bring atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבה's challenge from step 20. He shows that רבי יוסי's words do not have to mean that a חולין thought disqualifies the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה assumed there are only two options: either 'no intention' or 'disqualified.' אביי adds a middle level: כשר ואינו מרצה, meaning valid but not bringing atonement. So the difference רבי יוסי points to is only about atonement, not about being disqualified. רב's ruling that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of חולין is כשרה fits this, if we read it as valid but not bringing atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; maybe (opens a possible other reading)
Valid; the קרבן is not disqualified
Brings atonement or acceptance for the owner
Does not bring atonement, even though it is valid
In his heart; in his mind (his intention)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'valid' (כשר) with 'brings atonement' (מרצה). A קרבן can be כשר, so it is offered and not thrown out, and still not be מרצה, meaning the owner has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a three-level ladder for קרבנות: valid and bringing atonement, valid but not bringing atonement, and disqualified. Many later סוגיות use this ladder.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבה, who just raised the challenge from רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Perhaps he means: if there was no intention at all,
it is valid and brings atonement,
but if he had in mind 'for the sake of non-sacred,'
it is valid but does not bring atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge in step 20 by showing his inference from רבי יוסי is not forced.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: the difference רבי יוסי points to is about atonement (מרצה), not about being disqualified.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה thought רבי יוסי meant that a חולין intention disqualifies the קרבן, which would go against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חולין intention leaves the קרבן כשר but אינו מרצה. רב's word 'כשרה' can be read the same way: the חטאת is valid but does not bring atonement. So רבי יוסי does not contradict רב.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: 'For the Sake of' חולין vs. 'As' חולין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of חולין is valid. If it was slaughtered as חולין, really thinking it was ordinary, it is disqualified. The גמרא then sets up a supporting question from שמואל to רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A חטאת slaughtered for the sake of חולין is valid. If it was slaughtered as חולין, it is disqualified. This is like the question שמואל asked רב הונא:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר agrees with רב but adds an important distinction between two kinds of חולין thoughts. The last line sets up the next move: a question שמואל asked רב הונא, which the גמרא will bring next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לשם חולין' means he knows it is a חטאת and is just thinking about חולין. That thought cannot ruin it, as רב said. 'משום חולין' means he thinks the animal really is ordinary, so he is not doing a sacrificial act at all, and it becomes פסולה. The words 'כדבעא מיניה' tell us that a source supporting this distinction is about to be quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of חולין: he knows it is holy but has a חולין intention
As חולין: he mistakenly thinks the animal is ordinary
Disqualified
Like the question that he asked him (introduces a supporting case)

steps.confusionAlert: The two phrases look almost the same, but they mean opposite results. לשם חולין is valid. משום חולין, where he really thought it was ordinary, is disqualified.
steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction sets the limits of רב's rule. A חולין thought is harmless only when the person still knows he is doing a קרבן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
A sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of non-sacred is valid.
If he slaughtered it as non-sacred, it is disqualified.
This is like the question that Shmuel asked Rav Huna:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: חַטָּאת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ לְשֵׁם חוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב's ruling has been defended, רבי אלעזר narrows it by separating 'for the sake of חולין' from 'as חולין', and the גמרא sets up a supporting source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת slaughtered לשם חולין is כשרה. One slaughtered משום חולין, thinking it is truly ordinary, is פסולה.
